title: A universally tensor-weak comparison transfers the augmentation property
provenance: This run’s explicit scope correction; it does not change the frozen transcription or decide unseen ink.
statement: Let UW consist of maps f such that f tensor id_X belongs to W for every coefficient object X. If the augmented comparison between J and J-prime is itself in UW, and the augmentation of J is in UW, then the augmentation of J-prime is in UW. This holds in either comparison direction when the augmentation triangle commutes.
hypotheses: The tensor products and the augmentation triangle are defined.
W satisfies two-out-of-three.
Both the augmentation of J and the comparison map are universally tensor-weak.
justification: Tensor the commuting augmentation triangle with each X and apply composition or two-out-of-three in W.
scope_limit: Bicoaugmentations and a compatible comparison alone do not suffice. The saved counterexample has J-prime=J direct-sum Q[2] in nonnegative rational chain complexes; both comparison directions exist, but H_2(J-prime)=Q. The additional UW assumption is not claimed to appear in the manuscript.
reference_scope: GrothendieckPS2021 sections134 and138 supply the interval/linearization context. The additional UW hypothesis and its two-out-of-three proof are this run’s sufficient repair, not an assertion attributed to those sections.

title: The coefficient counit must be invertible
provenance: This run’s explicit scope correction; it does not change the frozen transcription or decide unseen ink.
statement: For T(V)=U tensor_k V and an adjunction L left-adjoint to T, invertibility of the counit epsilon_k:L(U) to k implies invertibility of every counit and therefore full faithfulness of T.
hypotheses: k is commutative and C is a locally small cocomplete k-linear abelian category.
T is the coefficient tensor functor and L is its k-linear left adjoint.
The counit epsilon_k is an isomorphism, not merely an existing arrow.
justification: Free presentations give L(U tensor V)=L(U) tensor V. Naturality identifies epsilon_V with epsilon_k tensor id_V. The adjunction criterion then gives full faithfulness.
scope_limit: The frozen premise displays an arrow without an isomorphism sign. For C=Mod_Q and U=Q^2, the evaluated object has dimension4 and its evaluation map to Q is not invertible.
reference_scope: Stacks0036, Lemma4.24.4 supplies the adjunction full-faithfulness criterion. The coefficient-presentation argument is reconstructed in the proof report; Freyd1964 supplies the surrounding adjoint-theorem context.

title: Quantify the rank test over every coefficient
provenance: This run’s explicit scope correction; it does not change the frozen transcription or decide unseen ink.
statement: For a finite projective module X over a commutative ring k, the coevaluation units are epic for every coefficient module, equivalently the evaluation counits are monic for every coefficient module, exactly when rank(X_p) is at most1 at every prime p. For one fixed coefficient A, impose that rank bound only at primes where A_p is nonzero.
hypotheses: X is finite projective over a commutative ring k.
The adjoints and unit/counit are the standard dual-basis tensor adjunctions.
The unrestricted iff is quantified over every coefficient module; testing A=k already detects failure.
justification: Locally, coevaluation is the diagonal vector in a free module of rank r^2 and evaluation is its transpose. Rank0 gives an epic map A to0 and a monic map0 to A; rank1 gives isomorphisms; at rank at least2 the complementary copies of a nonzero A prevent the stated epi/mono properties.
scope_limit: A=0 satisfies both tests at every rank and disproves a reading for an arbitrary single fixed coefficient without a support restriction. The finite Q-matrix computations illustrate the general local argument.
reference_scope: SGA6 I5.8.3 and the cited perfect-duality background support finite projectivity and duality. The rank-at-most-one criterion is proved by the local calculation in this run.

title: The unit kernel sequence needs an epic unit
provenance: This run’s explicit scope correction; it does not change the frozen transcription or decide unseen ink.
statement: In an abelian category, the sequence0 to ker(eta_x) to x to T L x to0 is short exact exactly when its final nonzero map eta_x is epic.
hypotheses: L is left-adjoint to T and eta_x:x to T L x is its unit.
The ambient category is abelian.
Epimorphy of eta_x is an additional condition when asserting the terminal0.
justification: Kernel exactness supplies the left part. Exactness at T L x is precisely surjectivity in the categorical, epic sense.
scope_limit: Existence of both adjoints does not guarantee epimorphy. Over Q, tensoring with Q^2 has unit Q to Q^4, which is not epic.
reference_scope: The short-exactness criterion is the direct kernel/image argument. Stacks0036 supplies the adjunction context, not a claim that all adjunction units are epic.

title: Reverse the dual formula only under reflexivity or a representing hypothesis
provenance: This run’s explicit scope correction; it does not change the frozen transcription or decide unseen ink.
statement: Adjunction gives (Lx)-dual = Hom_C(x,U). The reverse formula Lx = Hom_C(x,U)-dual holds if Lx is reflexive. It also follows directly when x is compact projective and Hom_C(x,U) is finite projective over k in the stated cocomplete k-linear setting.
hypotheses: L is left-adjoint to T(V)=U tensor_k V.
Either Lx is reflexive, or x is compact projective and H=Hom_C(x,U) is finite projective.
justification: The first option applies the bidual map. For the second, free presentations give Hom_C(x,U tensor V)=H tensor V=Hom_k(H-dual,V); Yoneda identifies Lx with H-dual.
scope_limit: Finite projectivity of Hom_C(x,U) alone is insufficient: C=Ab, U=Z, L=T=id, x=Z/2 gives a zero, hence finite-projective, dual but nonzero Lx. This does not refute the compact-projective case on scan79.
reference_scope: SGA6 I7.2–7.3 and Stacks07VI give the finite-projective/perfect setting. The compact-projective representability calculation and the torsion counterexample are checked explicitly in this run.

title: Restrict the chain-duality anti-equivalence
provenance: This run’s explicit scope correction; it does not change the frozen transcription or decide unseen ink.
statement: Ordinary degreewise duality, with the standard reversal of degrees, is an anti-equivalence on bounded complexes of finite projective k-modules. Derived duality R Hom_k(-,k) is an anti-equivalence on perfect complexes.
hypotheses: k is a commutative ring.
Use bounded degreewise finite-projective complexes for ordinary duality, or perfect objects for derived duality.
justification: Finite-projective evaluation maps identify each term with its bidual and respect the differentials. The perfect derived version is the cited theorem, separately from the elementary degreewise argument.
scope_limit: No anti-equivalence of all ordinary complexes of arbitrary modules follows. Z/2[0] has zero ordinary Z-dual. The manuscript’s uppercase/lowercase category notation remains an ink question.
reference_scope: SGA6 I, Proposition7.2, Definition7.3 and Corollary7.7; Stacks07VI. The ordinary bounded finite-projective bidual argument is supplied separately.

title: The proposed endpoint-collapsing map has a precise compatibility condition
provenance: This run’s explicit scope correction; it does not change the frozen transcription or decide unseen ink.
statement: For the displayed beta=delta_0 alpha lambda_!(epsilon), both source endpoints map to delta_0 alpha. This candidate preserves the two prescribed target endpoints exactly when delta_0 alpha = delta_1 alpha.
hypotheses: The displayed maps are defined and epsilon delta_i=id for i=0,1.
The target endpoint requirements are beta lambda_!(delta_i)=delta_i alpha.
justification: Substitute each endpoint into beta. Both composites equal delta_0 alpha, so only the second endpoint requirement imposes an additional equality.
scope_limit: This is a test of that candidate, not a construction of a replacement or an assertion that the author retracted it. For the standard two-endpoint example the matrix is [[1,1],[0,0]].
reference_scope: Direct substitution into the manuscript candidate; no external theorem is needed.

title: Symmetric stabilization under the cyclic-permutation condition
provenance: This run’s explicit scope correction; it does not change the frozen transcription or decide unseen ink.
statement: Retain the valid conditional: nonfaithfulness of the canonical comparison from ordinary suspension stabilization to monoidal object inversion would prevent the proposed compatible symmetric monoidal structure. When the cyclic3-permutation of Z tensor Z tensor Z is eventually the identity in the stabilization, the ordinary symmetric monoidal localization theorem supplies that structure and identifies the two universal constructions. For Z=S^1 in the usual pointed symmetric-smash homotopy category, this permutation is homotopic to identity, so the manuscript’s asserted nonfaithful example does not occur.
hypotheses: An ordinary symmetric monoidal category and stabilization by tensoring with Z, with the stated universal properties and usual size convention.
The cyclic3-permutation satisfies the eventual-identity condition of Voevodsky1998 Theorem4.3 / Robalo2015 Theorem2.14.
For the S^1 application, use the usual pointed homotopy category with its symmetric smash product; the groupoid input to the fraction construction must be specified.
justification: The conditional follows by constructing H from the monoidal universal property and obtaining HG naturally isomorphic to id from the ordinary suspension universal property. For S^1, the cyclic permutation on S^3 has degree+1; equivalently it is a120-degree rotation of R^3 extended over infinity, and a rotation homotopy fixes infinity. This verifies the exact hypothesis of the ordinary-category theorem.
scope_limit: The theorem has no finite-CW premise on other objects. This statement does not identify the formal stabilization of all spaces with the entire category of spectra. The theorem statement and application were checked; its complete published proof was not independently re-proved.
reference_scope: Voevodsky1998 Theorem4.3 p588; Robalo2015 Theorem2.14 pp445–446 and Remark2.15. FreydStable1966 section2 pp124–125 gives ordinary suspension and section4 p137 gives permutation signs.

title: A units-group bitorsor requires additional ring structure to represent a bimodule
provenance: This run’s explicit scope correction; it does not change the frozen transcription or decide unseen ink.
statement: Do not identify arbitrary O*-bitorsors with invertible unital O-bimodules. A comparison with bimodules must retain compatible additive and unital ring actions, or the corresponding Morita data; multiplicative unit actions alone are insufficient.
hypotheses: The proposed comparison concerns invertible unital bimodules over a ring or sheaf of rings.
A units-group bitorsor records commuting free transitive actions of O*, but does not itself specify the required addition or ring actions.
justification: Over the punctual topos with O=F5, take ordinary left multiplication on F5* and the right action x.u=x u^{-1}. This is a bitorsor. An invertible unital F5-bimodule is one-dimensional on the left and its right twist is a field automorphism; F5 has only the identity automorphism. Inversion fails additivity, since inv(2)=3 whereas inv(1)+inv(1)=2.
scope_limit: The record supplies a necessary scope correction and a fully checked counterexample. It does not assert an unrestricted equivalence between all ring-compatible torsor constructions and all Morita-invertible bimodules on arbitrary ringed topoi.
reference_scope: The counterexample and every bitorsor hypothesis are checked in root_proof_checks.md section5; no unrestricted classification theorem for arbitrary ringed topoi is inferred.
